newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian drug lord diversifies business.
newsitem.headline: Colombian drug lord diversifies business.

text.p: Jailed drug kingpin Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela has switched from trafficking cocaine to selling coffee and cookies to fellow inmates, a Colombian prison spokesman said on Tuesday.
And when not behind the counter of his kiosk in the yard of Bogota's La Picota maximum security jail, the self-confessed drug baron studies business administration and English.

That is not to say he and his brother Gilberto, alias the "chess player," also behind La Picota's bars since his capture last year, do not already know a thing or two about supply, demand and profit margins. As heads of the mighty Cali cartel the billionaire duo were responsible for supplying 80 percent of the world's cocaine, according to the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration.
A national prisons spokesman said Tuesday, "This type of work will change his life. It helps change his mentality and allows a person to develop other types of activity."
Nevertheless new deliveries of chocolate, soda and toilet paper are thoroughly checked "just to make sure the boxes are not filled with something else", the spokesman said.

U.S. officials said the Colombian government was too lenient with its drug traffickers and that they continued to head criminal mafias from jail. In response the Colombian authorities prepared a video showing the prison regime, which they hoped would calm the United States and pave the way for future cooperation from U.S. prison experts.
The scenes showing Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela and Gilberto, who also studies English, were edited from the final version but were leaked and broadcast by Colombian TV in recent days.
